AI.tldr: The paper presents a method to adapt the minimum-weight perfect matching algorithm for decoding bivariate bicycle codes by exploiting their equivalence to toric code copies, introducing a 'cylinder trick' for efficient correction, and benchmarking on various code families with competitive performance.
AI.motivation: New quantum error-correcting codes that encode multiple logical qubits into few physical qubits require efficient and accurate decoding methods. The minimum-weight perfect matching algorithm, valuable for topological codes, needs adaptation for bivariate bicycle codes.
AI.method: Adopt minimum-weight perfect matching algorithm for bivariate bicycle codes by exploiting their equivalence to copies of the toric code. Introduce the 'cylinder trick' to rapidly find corrections using matching on code symmetries. Augment matching with belief propagation and 'over-matching' strategies for improved performance.
AI.result: Benchmark the decoder on gross code family, cyclic hypergraph-product codes, generalized toric codes, and directional codes, demonstrating general applicability. For some codes, the augmented decoder achieves performance competitive with state-of-the-art approaches.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method successfully adapts minimum-weight perfect matching for bivariate bicycle codes, offering efficient decoding with competitive performance through the cylinder trick and augmentation strategies, applicable to various quantum error-correcting code families.

title: Optimization-based Unfolding in High-Energy Physics
summary: In High-Energy Physics, unfolding is the process of reconstructing true distributions of physical observables from detector-distorted measurements. Starting from its reformulation as a regularized quadratic optimization, we develop a framework to tackle this problem using both classical and quantum-compatible methods. In particular, we derive a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) representation of the unfolding objective, allowing direct implementation on quantum annealing and hybrid quantum-classical solvers. The proposed approach is implemented in QUnfold, an open-source Python package integrating classical mixed-integer solvers and D-Wave's hybrid quantum solver. We benchmark the method against widely used unfolding techniques in RooUnfold, including response Matrix Inversion, Iterative Bayesian Unfolding, and Singular Value Decomposition unfolding, using synthetic dataset with controlled distortion effects. Our results demonstrate that the optimization-based approach achieves competitive reconstruction accuracy across multiple distributions while naturally accommodating regularization within the objective function. This work establishes a unified optimization perspective on unfolding and provides a practical pathway for exploring quantum-enhanced methods in experimental HEP data analysis.

AI.tldr: The paper reformulates HEP unfolding as a regularized quadratic optimization problem, develops a QUBO representation for quantum implementation, creates the QUnfold package, and benchmarks it against classical methods showing competitive accuracy.
AI.motivation: High-Energy Physics unfolding reconstructs true distributions from detector-distorted measurements. The motivation is to establish a unified optimization framework that bridges classical and quantum approaches, enabling exploration of quantum-enhanced methods for HEP data analysis.
AI.method: Reformulates unfolding as regularized quadratic optimization, derives a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) representation compatible with quantum annealing and hybrid quantum-classical solvers. Implements approach in QUnfold Python package integrating classical mixed-integer solvers and D-Wave's hybrid quantum solver.
AI.result: Benchmarks against RooUnfold methods (Matrix Inversion, Iterative Bayesian Unfolding, SVD unfolding) using synthetic datasets with controlled distortion effects. The optimization-based approach achieves competitive reconstruction accuracy across multiple distributions while naturally accommodating regularization within the objective function.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a unified optimization perspective on unfolding and provides a practical pathway for exploring quantum-enhanced methods in experimental HEP data analysis. The QUBO representation enables direct implementation on quantum hardware while maintaining compatibility with classical solvers.

title: Generating entangled polaritonic condensates by pumping with entangled pairs of photons
summary: We investigate the steady state of two single-mode uniform spatially separated polaritonic conden- sates exposed to resonant pumping with entangled pairs of photons. We demonstrate the principal possibility of driving the system to an entangled state despite its exposure to noises arising from the excitonic reservoir and photon leakage through the microcavity mirrors. Estimates are provided for the flux of entangled particles required to drive the system into a steady state that violates the partial-transpose criterion for entanglement. Furthermore, we trace the evolution of the system after a sudden disappearance of the entangled pumping. Our analysis provides estimates for the entanglement lifetime in a system of two exciton-polariton condensates

AI.tldr: Two spatially separated polaritonic condensates can be driven to entangled steady states using resonant pumping with entangled photon pairs, despite noise sources, with estimates for required particle flux and entanglement lifetime.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether two spatially separated polaritonic condensates can achieve and maintain entanglement when exposed to resonant pumping with entangled photon pairs, despite the presence of noise from excitonic reservoirs and photon leakage.
AI.method: Analysis of steady states of two single-mode uniform spatially separated polaritonic condensates exposed to resonant pumping with entangled photon pairs, considering noise from excitonic reservoir and photon leakage through microcavity mirrors.
AI.result: Demonstrates principal possibility of driving the system to an entangled state despite noise, provides estimates for flux of entangled particles required to violate partial-transpose criterion, and traces evolution after sudden disappearance of entangled pumping.
AI.conclusion: The analysis shows that entangled steady states are achievable in polaritonic condensates with appropriate pumping, and provides estimates for entanglement lifetime in such systems.

title: No Absolute Hierarchy of Quantum Complementarity
comment: 4.25 pages (double column) + 6 pages (single column), 4 figures; Comments are welcome
summary: Bohr's principle of complementarity, prohibiting simultaneous access to certain physical properties within a single experimental arrangement, is considered to be a defining feature of quantum mechanics. It is commonly viewed as inducing an intrinsic hierarchy among incompatible observables: some sets of quantum properties are fundamentally more incompatible than others, as quantified by the maximal sharpness permitting their joint measurement. We show that this hierarchy ceases to be absolute in the multi-copy regime. Analyzing qubit spin observables, we prove a No-Comparison Theorem establishing that no global ordering of incompatible observable sets is preserved across all finite-copy configurations. In particular, two sets of observables can exhibit reversed complementarity ordering depending solely on whether the available resources are arranged as identical copies or as parallel-antiparallel pairs. Thus, the degree of quantum incompatibility is not an intrinsic property of observables alone but depends on the global configuration of the prepared quantum probes. Our results uncover a configuration-dependent structure of complementarity, reveal a subtle role of entanglement in shaping the structure of measurement limitations, and call for a reassessment of quantum information protocols under finite resources.

AI.tldr: No absolute hierarchy exists for incompatible quantum observables across multi-copy regimes; complementarity ordering can reverse depending on whether resources are arranged as identical copies or parallel-antiparallel pairs.
AI.motivation: Bohr's complementarity principle suggests an intrinsic hierarchy among incompatible quantum observables, with some sets being fundamentally more incompatible than others. The paper investigates whether this hierarchy remains absolute when considering multiple copies of quantum systems.
AI.method: Analysis of qubit spin observables with a No-Comparison Theorem proving that no global ordering of incompatible observable sets is preserved across all finite-copy configurations. Examines different resource arrangements: identical copies versus parallel-antiparallel pairs.
AI.result: Two sets of observables can exhibit reversed complementarity ordering depending solely on resource arrangement. The degree of quantum incompatibility is not intrinsic to observables alone but depends on the global configuration of prepared quantum probes.
AI.conclusion: Complementarity has a configuration-dependent structure, entanglement plays a subtle role in shaping measurement limitations, and quantum information protocols need reassessment under finite resources due to this non-absolute hierarchy.

title: Control of Multipartite Entanglement through Anisotropy against Thermal Noise
summary: Preserving multipartite entanglement in open many-body quantum systems is fundamentally limited by unavoidable environmental noise. We study the open-system dynamics of multipartite entanglement in an anisotropic XXZ spin chain interacting with a thermal spin bath, focusing on two states with distinct types of multipartite entanglement: the generalized GHZ and the generalized W state. Using a master-equation approach combined with the Bethe ansatz technique, we show analytically that robustness of multipartite entanglement at low temperatures can be enhanced by suitably tuning the anisotropy of the system. Our results highlight interaction-induced spectral control as a mechanism for stabilizing multipartite entanglement in quantum computing platforms.

AI.tldr: Anisotropic XXZ spin chain interacting with thermal bath shows that tuning anisotropy can enhance robustness of multipartite entanglement (GHZ and W states) at low temperatures via interaction-induced spectral control.
AI.motivation: Preserving multipartite entanglement in open many-body quantum systems is fundamentally limited by unavoidable environmental noise, requiring mechanisms to stabilize entanglement for quantum computing applications.
AI.method: Master-equation approach combined with Bethe ansatz technique to study open-system dynamics of multipartite entanglement in anisotropic XXZ spin chain interacting with thermal spin bath, analyzing generalized GHZ and generalized W states.
AI.result: Robustness of multipartite entanglement at low temperatures can be enhanced by suitably tuning the anisotropy of the system, demonstrating interaction-induced spectral control as a stabilization mechanism.
AI.conclusion: Interaction-induced spectral control provides a mechanism for stabilizing multipartite entanglement in quantum computing platforms, with anisotropy tuning offering a practical approach to enhance entanglement robustness against thermal noise.

title: Hyperbolic and Semi-Hyperbolic Floquet Codes for Photonic Quantum Computing
summary: Tailoring error correcting codes to the structure of the physical noise can reduce the overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation. Hyperbolic Floquet codes use only weight-2 measurements and can be implemented directly on hardware with native pair measurements. We construct hyperbolic and semi-hyperbolic Floquet codes from $\{8,3\}$, $\{10,3\}$, and $\{12,3\}$ tessellations via the Wythoff kaleidoscopic construction with the Low-Index Normal Subgroups (LINS) algorithm. The $\{10,3\}$ and $\{12,3\}$ families are new to hyperbolic Floquet codes. We evaluate these codes under four noise models: phenomenological, ancilla Entangling Measurement (EM3), Single-step Depolarizing EM3 (SDEM3), and erasure. Under phenomenological noise, specific-logical threshold crossings occur near $p_e \approx 0.3$--$0.5\%$ for $\{8,3\}$ ($k=6$--$56$) and $0.15$--$0.2\%$ for $\{10,3\}$ ($k=12$--$146$). EM3 ancilla noise yields a threshold of ${\sim}1.5\%$ for all three families. SDEM3 is a depolarizing noise model motivated by Majorana tetron architectures; fine-grained codes achieve thresholds of ${\sim}1.0$--$1.2\%$ for all three families. The erasure model captures detected photon loss on spin-optical links; fine-grained codes achieve erasure thresholds of ${\sim}8.5$--$9\%$ for $\{8,3\}$, ${\sim}7$--$8\%$ for $\{10,3\}$, and ${\sim}6.5$--$8\%$ for $\{12,3\}$. Photon loss is the dominant error source in photon-mediated quantum computing. Under the full three-parameter SPOQC-2 noise model, the $\{8,3\}$ codes achieve a 2D fault-tolerant area $2.2\times$ that of the surface code compiled to pair measurements while encoding $k = 10$ logical qubits. In a companion paper, we evaluate the same code families in a distributed setting.

AI.tldr: Hyperbolic Floquet codes constructed from {8,3}, {10,3}, and {12,3} tessellations show improved fault tolerance under various noise models, with {8,3} codes achieving 2.2× better area efficiency than surface codes while encoding 10 logical qubits.
AI.motivation: To reduce overhead in fault-tolerant quantum computation by tailoring error correcting codes to physical noise structure, specifically using hyperbolic Floquet codes that only require weight-2 measurements and can be implemented directly on hardware with native pair measurements.
AI.method: Construct hyperbolic and semi-hyperbolic Floquet codes from {8,3}, {10,3}, and {12,3} tessellations using the Wythoff kaleidoscopic construction with the Low-Index Normal Subgroups (LINS) algorithm. Evaluate codes under four noise models: phenomenological, ancilla Entangling Measurement (EM3), Single-step Depolarizing EM3 (SDEM3), and erasure.
AI.result: Under phenomenological noise: thresholds of 0.3-0.5% for {8,3} (k=6-56) and 0.15-0.2% for {10,3} (k=12-146). EM3 ancilla noise: ~1.5% threshold for all families. SDEM3: ~1.0-1.2% thresholds. Erasure model: ~8.5-9% for {8,3}, ~7-8% for {10,3}, ~6.5-8% for {12,3}. Under SPOQC-2 noise model, {8,3} codes achieve 2.2× better fault-tolerant area than surface codes while encoding k=10 logical qubits.
AI.conclusion: Hyperbolic Floquet codes, particularly those constructed from {8,3} tessellations, offer significant advantages for fault-tolerant quantum computation by providing better area efficiency and noise resilience compared to surface codes, especially in architectures with native pair measurements and photon-mediated quantum computing.

title: Coherence squeezing in optical interference
summary: We introduce the concept of optical coherence squeezing in double-slit interference. We construct Hermitian operators that characterize the coherence at the slits, leading to coherence uncertainty relations and a corresponding squeezing condition. We also analyze states exhibiting such squeezing and show its manifestations in the uncertainty of the magnitudes and positions of the intensity fringes. Our work identifies coherence as a fundamental degree of freedom for squeezing, complementing phase, amplitude, and polarization, which could benefit quantum-enhanced interferometry.

AI.tldr: Optical coherence squeezing in double-slit interference is introduced as a new degree of freedom for squeezing, with uncertainty relations for coherence operators and observable effects on interference fringe properties.
AI.motivation: To identify coherence as a fundamental degree of freedom for squeezing that complements existing squeezing types (phase, amplitude, polarization) and could enhance quantum interferometry applications.
AI.method: Construct Hermitian operators characterizing coherence at double slits, derive coherence uncertainty relations, establish squeezing conditions, and analyze states exhibiting coherence squeezing to study effects on interference fringe properties.
AI.result: Demonstrated coherence squeezing as a new squeezing type with corresponding uncertainty relations, identified states exhibiting this squeezing, and showed its manifestations in intensity fringe magnitude and position uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: Coherence is established as a fundamental squeezing degree of freedom alongside phase, amplitude, and polarization, with potential applications in quantum-enhanced interferometry through manipulation of interference fringe properties.

title: A quantum feasibility preserving modeling for the min cut problem
summary: We study the minimum cut problem in weighted undirected graphs using variational quantum algorithms in which only feasible cut configurations are explored. Although minimum cut admits efficient classical solutions, it is a fundamental component of more complex network optimization problems such as multicut and network interdiction. Our objective is to examine quantum models in which feasibility is preserved by the mixer dynamics, without introducing penalty terms in the cost Hamiltonian. We employ a ring structured XY mixer that restricts the quantum evolution to the subspace of valid cut configurations, ensuring that all sampled states correspond to feasible solutions. To address scalability limitations, we suggest an iterative metaheuristic strategy that decomposes large instances into smaller subproblems solved sequentially using the same quantum model. The results obtained using the mixer indicate that the initial probability distribution can be systematically controlled, thereby enabling the development of warm start techniques within variational quantum based algorithms.

AI.tldr: Quantum variational algorithm for minimum cut using XY mixer to preserve feasibility without penalty terms, with iterative metaheuristic for scalability and warm-start techniques.
AI.motivation: Minimum cut is fundamental for complex network optimization problems (multicut, network interdiction). The paper aims to examine quantum models that preserve feasibility through mixer dynamics rather than penalty terms, exploring quantum advantage for combinatorial optimization.
AI.method: Uses variational quantum algorithms with ring-structured XY mixer that restricts evolution to valid cut configurations subspace. Proposes iterative metaheuristic strategy decomposing large instances into smaller subproblems solved sequentially with same quantum model.
AI.result: The mixer enables systematic control of initial probability distribution, allowing development of warm-start techniques within variational quantum algorithms. Feasibility is preserved without penalty terms in cost Hamiltonian.
AI.conclusion: Quantum models with feasibility-preserving mixers offer promising approach for combinatorial optimization, with warm-start techniques and iterative decomposition addressing scalability limitations for practical applications.

title: Cryptographic Fragility of Standard Quantum Repeater Protocols
summary: The security of the proposed quantum Internet relies on repeater protocols designed under the assumption of stochastic, characterizable noise. We demonstrate that in adversarial environments this assumption induces performance vulnerabilities for computationally bounded repeater nodes. We show that the standard BBPSSW distillation protocol recursively purifies error syndromes rather than entanglement. This leads to a state of low fidelity despite diagnostic metrics indicating perfect convergence. Moreover, we show that the verifier cannot check the adversarial influence via the maximum likelihood estimation algorithm since it is blind to computationally bounded observers. To address these vulnerabilities, we propose a Cryptographic Network Stack centered on a trapdoor verification protocol. The protocol exploits private randomness to restore operational stability without requiring channel characterization.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies security vulnerabilities in quantum repeater protocols under adversarial conditions, showing that standard distillation protocols can be manipulated to produce low-fidelity states while appearing successful, and proposes a cryptographic solution with trapdoor verification.
AI.motivation: Current quantum Internet security relies on repeater protocols assuming stochastic, characterizable noise, but this assumption creates vulnerabilities in adversarial environments where attackers can exploit computational limitations of repeater nodes.
AI.method: The authors analyze the BBPSSW distillation protocol, demonstrating it recursively purifies error syndromes rather than entanglement, and show that maximum likelihood estimation is blind to computationally bounded observers. They propose a Cryptographic Network Stack with a trapdoor verification protocol using private randomness.
AI.result: The analysis reveals that adversarial manipulation can lead to low-fidelity quantum states despite diagnostic metrics indicating perfect convergence, and that standard verification methods cannot detect such attacks. The proposed cryptographic solution restores operational stability without requiring channel characterization.
AI.conclusion: Quantum repeater protocols designed for stochastic noise environments are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that exploit computational limitations. A cryptographic approach with trapdoor verification using private randomness is necessary to secure quantum networks against such threats.

title: Geometric control of maximal entanglement via bound states in the continuum
summary: Bound states in the continuum (BiCs) convert dissipative open systems into effectively closed quantum subspaces through destructive interference. We show that two identical giant atoms coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide support BICs that coincide with maximally entangled atomic states. Most importantly, entanglement is predominantly determined by the geometric design; the ratio of intra-atomic connection lengths fixes the concurrence, while the propagation phase between atoms selects a family of Bell-like states. We further analyze the dynamical stability of these maximally entangled BICs under exact time evolution, revealing a clear hierarchy of robustness against parameter perturbations. Our results establish an analytical bridge between symmetry, geometry, entanglement, and BICs in giant-atom waveguide platforms.

AI.tldr: Giant atoms coupled to waveguides can form bound states in the continuum (BICs) that correspond to maximally entangled atomic states, with entanglement determined by geometric design parameters.
AI.motivation: To establish connections between symmetry, geometry, entanglement, and bound states in the continuum (BICs) in quantum waveguide platforms with giant atoms, and to understand how geometric design can control entanglement properties.
AI.method: Study two identical giant atoms coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide, analyze BIC formation, examine how geometric parameters (intra-atomic connection lengths and propagation phase between atoms) determine entanglement, and investigate dynamical stability through exact time evolution analysis.
AI.result: BICs coincide with maximally entangled atomic states; concurrence is fixed by ratio of intra-atomic connection lengths; propagation phase selects Bell-like state family; dynamical stability analysis reveals hierarchy of robustness against parameter perturbations.
AI.conclusion: Establishes analytical bridge between symmetry, geometry, entanglement, and BICs in giant-atom waveguide platforms, demonstrating geometric control over entanglement properties and stability of quantum states.

title: Q-Tag: Watermarking Quantum Circuit Generative Models
summary: Quantum cloud platforms have become the most widely adopted and mainstream approach for accessing quantum computing resources, due to the scarcity and operational complexity of quantum hardware. In this service-oriented paradigm, quantum circuits, which constitute high-value intellectual property, are exposed to risks of unauthorized access, reuse, and misuse. Digital watermarking has been explored as a promising mechanism for protecting quantum circuits by embedding ownership information for tracing and verification. However, driven by recent advances in generative artificial intelligence, the paradigm of quantum circuit design is shifting from individually and manually constructed circuits to automated synthesis based on quantum circuit generative models (QCGMs). In such generative settings, protecting only individual output circuits is insufficient, and existing post hoc, circuit-centric watermarking methods are not designed to integrate with the generative process, often failing to simultaneously ensure stealthiness, functional correctness, and robustness at scale. These limitations highlight the need for a new watermarking paradigm that is natively integrated with quantum circuit generative models. In this work, we present the first watermarking framework for QCGMs, which embeds ownership signals into the generation process while preserving circuit fidelity. We introduce a symmetric sampling strategy that aligns watermark encoding with the model's Gaussian prior, and a synchronization mechanism that counteracts adversarial watermark attack through latent drift correction. Empirical results confirm that our method achieves high-fidelity circuit generation and robust watermark detection across a range of perturbations, paving the way for scalable, secure copyright protection in AI-powered quantum design.

AI.tldr: First watermarking framework for quantum circuit generative models that embeds ownership signals during generation while preserving circuit fidelity, using symmetric sampling and latent drift correction for robustness.
AI.motivation: Quantum cloud platforms expose quantum circuits (high-value IP) to unauthorized access/reuse risks. Existing circuit-centric watermarking methods are insufficient for generative AI settings where circuits are synthesized automatically, failing to ensure stealthiness, functional correctness, and robustness at scale.
AI.method: Introduces a watermarking framework natively integrated with quantum circuit generative models (QCGMs). Uses symmetric sampling strategy to align watermark encoding with the model's Gaussian prior, and a synchronization mechanism with latent drift correction to counteract adversarial attacks.
AI.result: Empirical results confirm the method achieves high-fidelity circuit generation and robust watermark detection across a range of perturbations, enabling scalable copyright protection in AI-powered quantum design.
AI.conclusion: The framework paves the way for scalable, secure copyright protection in AI-powered quantum design by providing the first watermarking solution specifically designed for quantum circuit generative models.

title: Connecting Quantum Contextuality and Nonlocality
summary: Quantum theory departs from classical physics in its treatment of correlations, most prominently through the phenomena of contextuality and nonlocality. Once regarded primarily as foundational curiosities, these effects are now understood as key operational resources for quantum computation, communication, and simulation. Although traditionally investigated in distinct settings, recent theoretical and experimental advances have revealed deep conceptual, mathematical, and operational connections between them. This review presents a unified perspective on these developments based on sheaf-theoretic and graph-theoretic frameworks, which provide theory-independent characterizations of statistical correlations. These approaches clarify the structural relationship between contextuality and nonlocality, facilitate the formulation of experimentally testable inequalities, and guide implementations in realistic physical platforms, with particular emphasis on photonic systems. By bridging abstract theoretical structures and concrete experimental realizations, this review sheds light on the nonclassical foundations of quantum correlations and their emerging role in quantum technologies.

AI.tldr: This review paper presents a unified perspective on quantum contextuality and nonlocality using sheaf-theoretic and graph-theoretic frameworks, connecting these foundational concepts to practical quantum technologies.
AI.motivation: To bridge the gap between foundational quantum phenomena (contextuality and nonlocality) and their practical applications in quantum technologies, and to provide a unified theoretical framework for understanding these correlations.
AI.method: Uses sheaf-theoretic and graph-theoretic frameworks to provide theory-independent characterizations of statistical correlations, enabling structural analysis of contextuality-nonlocality relationships and formulation of experimentally testable inequalities.
AI.result: The frameworks clarify structural relationships between contextuality and nonlocality, facilitate creation of testable inequalities, and guide implementations in physical platforms (particularly photonic systems), bridging abstract theory with experimental realizations.
AI.conclusion: The review demonstrates how foundational quantum correlations (contextuality and nonlocality) have evolved from theoretical curiosities to operational resources for quantum technologies, with unified mathematical frameworks enabling practical applications and deeper understanding of quantum foundations.

title: Quantum diffusion for a quantum particle with a correlated Gaussian noise
summary: We investigate the diffusive behavior of a quantum particle driven by a correlated Gaussian noise. We derive the analytical solution of the joint probability density function and obtain explicit expressions for the mean square momentum and the mean square displacement.

AI.tldr: Analytical study of quantum particle diffusion under correlated Gaussian noise, deriving joint probability density and explicit expressions for momentum and displacement statistics.
AI.motivation: To understand the diffusive behavior of quantum particles subjected to correlated Gaussian noise, which is relevant for quantum transport, Brownian motion in quantum systems, and noise-driven quantum dynamics.
AI.method: Derived analytical solution for the joint probability density function using mathematical techniques for correlated Gaussian noise processes, obtaining explicit expressions for statistical moments.
AI.result: Obtained analytical expressions for mean square momentum and mean square displacement, characterizing the diffusive behavior of the quantum particle under correlated noise.
AI.conclusion: The study provides analytical tools to quantify quantum diffusion under correlated Gaussian noise, with implications for understanding quantum transport phenomena and noise effects in quantum systems.

title: Polarization-selective quantum cooperative response in dual-species atom arrays
summary: Atom arrays have emerged as a powerful platform for quantum light-matter interfaces, yet single-species arrays are constrained by in-plane symmetry, restricting polarization control. Here we investigate the cooperative optical response of dual-species subwavelength atom arrays, in which intrinsic polarizability difference breaks in-plane symmetry. By engineering the lattice spacing and detunings, the arrays exhibit polarization-dependent subradiant modes, enabling complete reflection of specific polarization component. Leveraging this mechanism, we assemble array units as functional pixels and demonstrate a scalable polarization-selective quantum light modulator. Our work establishes a dynamically reconfigurable atomic-photonic platform for versatile subwavelength quantum optical elements.

AI.tldr: Dual-species atom arrays break in-plane symmetry to enable polarization-dependent subradiant modes and complete reflection of specific polarizations, creating a scalable polarization-selective quantum light modulator.
AI.motivation: Single-species atom arrays are limited by in-plane symmetry constraints that restrict polarization control, creating a need for platforms that can manipulate light polarization at the quantum level.
AI.method: Use dual-species subwavelength atom arrays where intrinsic polarizability differences break in-plane symmetry. Engineer lattice spacing and detunings to create polarization-dependent subradiant modes that completely reflect specific polarization components.
AI.result: Arrays exhibit polarization-dependent subradiant modes enabling complete reflection of specific polarization components. Array units function as pixels to create a scalable polarization-selective quantum light modulator.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes a dynamically reconfigurable atomic-photonic platform for versatile subwavelength quantum optical elements with polarization control capabilities.
